findings: The common name, scientific name, and family are correctly shown as Northern Rough-winged Swallow, Stelgidopteryx serripennis, and Hirundinidae; All About Birds, Audubon, and eBird independently confirm the identity.

All printed measurements exactly match All About Birds: length 12–15 cm (4.7–5.9 in), weight 10–18 g (0.3–0.6 oz), and wingspan 27–30 cm (10.6–11.8 in). Audubon independently confirms the length and wingspan while publishing a narrower weight range of 11–14 g.
Every habitat and behavior line matches the proposed text without duplicated, omitted, substituted, or nonsensical words. The claims are supported by the direct source pages.

All six printed field-mark statements match the proposed wording and verified identification traits: plain brown upperparts, diffuse dingy throat and chest, pale belly, small head and bill, long broad-based pointed wings, short square or slightly notched tail, and dark legs and feet.

The primary specimen agrees with the reference photographs in its unpatterned brown upperparts, gradual gray-brown-to-whitish underpart transition, dark eye and bill, compact tail, and dark feet. Its head and eye are slightly more rounded and prominent than in the clearest photographs, but not enough to create a conflicting species identity.

The folded primary wing and detached wing study both communicate a long, relatively broad, tapered and pointed swallow wing. The detached study is clearly supplementary and does not appear attached to the primary specimen.

The tail is short, nearly square-ended, and shallowly notched. Both legs and grasping feet are present without obvious duplication or malformation. The single lateral primary specimen has one head, one bill, two legs, one tail, and anatomically normal paired-wing organization, with the far wing naturally occluded.
The detached bill/head study is internally consistent with the primary head. Unequal mandible length is not an established field mark requiring a projected lower mandible for this species.

The body-length diagram is internally consistent: 12 cm is at the bottom, 15 cm is at the top, values increase upward, units and endpoints match the published range, and exactly four evenly spaced unlabeled interior ticks divide the range into five proportional segments. “SCHEMATIC — NOT TO SCALE” clearly prevents interpretation as the printed bird’s physical scale.
The plate is clean, legible, balanced, and uses the supplementary studies effectively without confusing them with additional birds.
No place name, ZIP code, coordinates, map, or local-observation detail appears anywhere on the plate.
